_comment: Functions that ARE compiler output and should match, but have not yet.
They are held out of the work queue so waves stop rediscovering them,
and they are deliberately NOT counted as progress anywhere: a parked
function is still assembly, the ROM is still built from its asm/ unit,
and the C in work/<fn>/ does not go into src/decomp/.
This is a different claim from data/asm-resident.json. That file says
'no C will ever match this, because a compiler did not write it'.
This file says 'C should match this and ours does not yet'. Do not put
an entry here in asm-resident.json to get it out of the queue -- that
file is the evidence base for what hand-written assembly looks like,
and a wrong entry poisons every later judgement made from it.
An entry needs three things in its reason field: the best percentage
reached, the EXACT remaining difference, and the axes already ruled out.
Without the ruled-out list the next wave repeats the same attempts --
which is the specific failure this file exists to prevent.
Before parking anything, check the toolchain axis. The ROM was built
with two compilers and more than one flag set, and three functions were
parked as source-exhausted across two waves and permuter runs when the
source was never the axis. See data/compiler-overrides.json and the
'Per-file compiler and flags' section of docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
Unparking is the goal. Re-run `python tools/trymatch.py <fn>` against a
parked entry whenever a new codegen rule lands; the draft is kept at
work/<fn>/<fn>.c and best.c holds the closest attempt.

functions.sub_0801A6C0: 98.4% -- 64 bytes, size-exact, ONE byte differs at +0x2a. The original stores `strh r2, [r1, #0]`; every candidate produces `strh r3, [r1, #0]`. Both registers hold 0 at that point (r2 was just zeroed and stored to [r1, #4], r3 likewise), so this is a pure register-allocation tie-break with no source-level lever on it -- the instruction selection, the order and every other byte are already correct. Ruled out: the source axis, exhaustively, across two waves plus decomp-permuter runs; and the toolchain axis -- old_agbcc and dropping -fforce-addr were both tried after the wave-10 two-compiler finding and neither moves this byte. Not every allocation near-miss is a flag problem. Worth re-testing whenever a register-allocation rule lands in docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
functions.sub_0805CA60:
99.5%% -- 188 bytes, size-exact, EVERY instruction and EVERY register identical to the ROM. The one differing byte is at +0x9c: the addend inside the second literal-pool word. Both pool words relocate against `.rodata` (+0 and +4) instead of against gUnknown_0816D9E0 / gUnknown_0816D9E4, and trymatch's reloc_equivalent cannot resolve a section symbol to an address, so it reports the addend as a byte diff.

This is a HARNESS limit, not a codegen miss, and the cause is understood: 0x0816D9E0-0x0816DA37 is agbcc's own .rodata address-constant pool, not a table of globals. -fforce-addr needs &gUnknown_030046B0 and gUnknown_030045F0 live across the builder's loop, so agbcc parks both addresses in .rodata and loads them through it; the ROM did exactly that, one pair per builder, thirteen pairs in function address order, every even slot 0x030046B0 and every odd slot 0x030045F0. sub_0805CDF0 and sub_0805CE20 -- the two builders with no loop -- have no pair, which pins the rule. The draft in work/<fn>/ is therefore almost certainly the original source verbatim; closing it needs the whole translation unit placed so its .rodata lands at 0x0816D9E0, which no per-function check can see.

Ruled out, all probed side by side (see docs/agbcc-codegen.md, 'The .rodata address-constant reroute'): declaring gUnknown_0816D9E0/E4 as `u8 **const` / `u8 *const` globals -- that keeps the relocation checkable and reaches the exact instruction multiset, but leaves the `adds r6, r3, #0` copy 4th in the loop preheader where the ROM has it last, 8 bytes, and NO source spelling moves it (the same extra locals, the same tail temp, an explicit `if` guard, a do/while(0) body and a `**pp` spelling with no locals at all were each tried; adding all of them to the DIRECT spelling leaves the copy last, so the ordering is decided by whether the address word is a constant-pool entry, not by the source). Also ruled out as the cause of the reroute: `const` on the globals (a non-const pair reroutes identically) and the number of references (two refs on the same side of the loop do not reroute; one either side does).
